name: Digispot AI – AI SEO Tools, Audit & MCP AI Agent
author: Digispot AI

sections.description:
Audit every page. Fix issues in bulk with AI. Let Claude or Cursor work on your SEO, with your approval. All inside wp-admin, free.

Search now happens in Google and in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude and Copilot. Digispot AI helps you win both.

→ See it: the Overview

✔ Free, no account needed

  • AI agents (MCP) that propose SEO fixes for your approval, with one-click undo
  • Bulk AI fixes with your own OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini or DeepSeek key
  • Keyword tracking from your own Search Console
  • Broken link checker and internal link suggestions
  • SEO change history with one-click undo for every change
  • Multi-location local SEO with LocalBusiness schema
  • Verified crawl log that catches fake Googlebots, and can block them if you choose
  • AI referrals from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Mode, Gemini and Copilot
  • Smart 404 monitor and unlimited redirects

Several of these are paid add-ons in other SEO plugins.

Overview: your site at a glance

  • A plain-language summary of what is going well and what needs attention
  • Clicks, searches by position, pages in Google, visits and key events, each compared with the previous 28 days
  • The next fixes ranked by impact, with site health and page audit scores side by side
  • Crawler visits, AI assistant visits, fixes made this month and unresolved 404s, each opening the exact list behind it

→ See it: the Overview

Switching from Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress or Redirection?

Import titles, descriptions, keywords, canonicals, robots, social fields, schema and redirects in one click. Safe to re-run. Never overwrites what you already set, and one click undoes the whole import.

→ See it: one-click migration

AI Agent (MCP): your AI assistant, your rules

  • Connect Claude, Cursor or another MCP app in a few steps, with a dedicated agent account you can revoke anytime
  • Agents read your audit, Search Console and Site Graph data, then propose fixes: titles, descriptions, alt text, internal links, redirects and schema
  • Every change waits for your approval with a before-and-after preview, unless you choose otherwise
  • Guardrails: change limits per agent, protected pages, email alerts and a full activity log

→ See it: agent approvals

SEO Audit: a score for every page

  • 75+ checks per page (grouped into audit packs), from meta tags and headings to speed, HTTPS and schema
  • Scores the rendered page, so Elementor and page-builder content counts
  • One ranked list of the issues costing you the most, across every page, under SEO Audit → Issues
  • Change history: every SEO change, whoever made it, with one-click undo

→ See it: the SEO audit · → See it: change history

AI Fixes: one click, you review

Fix issues straight from SEO Audit → Issues.

  • Titles, descriptions, focus keywords, alt text, schema, canonicals and H1s
  • Fix one page or every affected page at once
  • See each suggestion next to the current value. Nothing saves until you click Apply.

→ See it: bulk AI fixes

Search Console and GA4, inside WordPress

  • One-click Google connection, no Client ID to paste
  • Clicks, impressions, CTR and position next to GA4 sessions and channels, under Analytics → Google Insights
  • Keyword tracking in Search & AI → Keywords: pick your keywords and see position, clicks and what moved, free
  • SEO report by email, weekly or monthly (turn on in Settings → Modules)

→ See it: keyword tracking · → See it: Google Insights

Links that work for you

  • Internal link suggestions with the exact sentence and words, added in one click
  • Broken links checked in the background, with one-click fixes, under SEO Audit → Links
  • Site Structure (beta): see topic clusters, pillar pages and orphan pages on one map

→ See it: link suggestions · → See it: broken links · → See it: Site Structure

Search Appearance: titles, schema and local SEO

Everything you set once for how the site shows in search lives in Search Appearance: titles and meta templates, site identity and schema, local SEO and llms.txt.

  • Organization or LocalBusiness (55 types), WebSite, BreadcrumbList and page schema like Article, Product, FAQ, HowTo and Video
  • One profile per location with hours, services and payments
  • Graph, list and raw JSON-LD views with one-click copy

→ See it: schema markup · → See it: local SEO profiles

Editor panel

  • Live SEO score, focus and secondary keywords, snippet preview and social cards
  • “Generate with AI” for title and description
  • Works in the block editor, Classic editor, Elementor and Quick Edit

→ See it: the editor panel

Built for AI search

  • Search & AI → AI Visibility: which AI crawlers can reach you, AI visits, llms.txt and agent access on one screen
  • See every crawler visit: Googlebot, Bingbot, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and more
  • Crawlers verified against their published IP lists, so fakes are flagged with the network and country they really came from
  • See humans arriving from AI answers, with landing page and query
  • Auto-generated llms.txt (turn on in Settings → Modules)

→ See it: AI visibility · → See it: the verified crawl log · → See it: AI referrals

Technical SEO, handled

  • Redirects: 301, 302, 307, 308, 410 and 451, regex-capable, with hit counts, scheduling and CSV import/export
  • 404 monitor that separates real missing pages from bot probes
  • XML sitemaps, robots.txt editor, IndexNow, breadcrumbs and automatic image alt text

→ See it: redirects and the 404 monitor

For teams

  • Setup wizard: import, first audit and AI provider in a few steps
  • “SEO Manager” role for editors, without full admin access
  • Runs side by side with Yoast, Rank Math, AIOSEO or SEOPress without duplicate tags
  • WP-CLI commands for audits, SEO fields, redirects and undo
  • Turn modules on or off to load only what you use

Works with your stack

WordPress 6.2+, PHP 7.4+, block editor, Classic editor, WooCommerce and Elementor.

Free vs. Digispot Cloud

Everything above is free and runs in your WordPress site, including the AI agent, its approvals and undo. A free Digispot AI account adds managed AI credits (no AI key needed) and cloud lookups: search demand, Core Web Vitals field data and domain age.

Digispot AI Pro adds rank tracking, AI answer tracking, competitors, backlinks and exact keyword data to Search & AI, and gives your AI agent read-only tools for that data. Pro is a separate add-on, included in every paid Digispot AI plan with no separate purchase. You can hide its tabs in Settings → Pro.

Trademarks

Rank Math, Yoast SEO, All in One SEO (AIOSEO), SEOPress, WooCommerce, Elementor, Google, Google Search Console, Google Analytics, ChatGPT, OpenAI, Anthropic, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Microsoft Copilot, Bing and DeepSeek are trademarks of their respective owners. They are named only to describe compatibility, data import and integrations. Digispot AI is not affiliated with, sponsored by or endorsed by any of them.

Third-Party Services

This plugin relies on the following third-party services. Each entry states what is
sent and when. No data leaves your site until you connect or configure the relevant
service.

  1. Digispot AI API (https://api.digispot.ai, keyword and search data on https://app.digispot.ai, OAuth proxy https://wordpress.digispot.ai):
    Powers managed AI generation, rank tracking, backlink data, and the free lookups (keyword
    demand, Chrome UX Report web vitals, domain age, PageSpeed). Page content, titles, and prompts
    are sent only when you run an AI action or a cloud-backed report; keywords you research or set
    as focus keywords, your Search Console query strings, and your site’s URLs are sent only for
    those lookups. All of this happens only after you connect a Digispot account, and answers are
    cached in your WordPress database to avoid repeat calls. Every request from a connected site
    also carries your site’s address (domain), its Site Title and the plugin and WordPress version
    numbers, so your account can tell its connected sites apart. The OAuth proxy is contacted only during Google sign-in,
    so you never have to paste a Google Client ID. When an AI app connects with one-URL sign-in and your host
    keeps /.well-known away from WordPress, the app is pointed to the same host, which reads this site’s
    public sign-in details (endpoint addresses only); approvals and tokens stay on your site.

* Digispot Terms of Service
* Digispot Privacy Policy

  1. Google APIs (OAuth 2.0):
    Displays your Search Console, Analytics 4 (including visits by channel and city), and Business Profile data. Contacted only after
    you complete the Google OAuth flow. Retrieved data is stored locally in your WordPress
    database to speed up loading. Hosts used: accounts.google.com (sign-in),
    www.googleapis.com (Search Console), analyticsdata.googleapis.com and
    analyticsadmin.googleapis.com (Analytics 4), mybusiness.googleapis.com,
    mybusinessaccountmanagement.googleapis.com,
    mybusinessbusinessinformation.googleapis.com and
    businessprofileperformance.googleapis.com (Business Profile).

* Google Privacy Policy
* Google Terms of Service

  1. AI providers (opt-in, bring your own key):
    Digispot AI supports using your own API key with an external AI provider instead of the
    managed Digispot service. No content is sent to any of these providers until you
    explicitly select one and enter your own API key.     When enabled, the content you ask the
    plugin to optimize (such as a post title, excerpt, or body) is sent to the provider you
    chose:

* OpenAI – https://api.openai.com – Terms | Privacy
* Anthropic – https://api.anthropic.com – Terms | Privacy
* Google Gemini – https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com – Terms | Privacy
* DeepSeek – https://api.deepseek.com – Terms | Privacy

  1. IndexNow (https://api.indexnow.org):
    If you enable IndexNow, the URLs of posts you publish or update are POSTed to the IndexNow
    API so participating search engines can recrawl them. Only URLs and your generated
    IndexNow key are sent – never page content.

* IndexNow Documentation and Terms

  1. Anonymous usage telemetry (opt-in, OFF by default) (https://api.digispot.ai):
    If — and only if — you switch this on in the plugin settings, Digispot AI reports three
    lifecycle events (plugin activated, deactivated, uninstalled) so we can see how many sites
    use the plugin and why people stop. When you deactivate, you may optionally pick a reason;
    that reason is sent with the event. Nothing is sent while this setting is off, which is
    how it ships.     What is sent: an opaque random install identifier, the event name, and the
    plugin, WordPress and PHP version numbers. What is never sent: your site URL, your email,
    usernames, post content, or any other data that identifies you or your site.

* Digispot Terms of Service
* Digispot Privacy Policy

  1. Crawler IP range lists and IP network lookups (crawl log module only):
    The crawl log module downloads the IP-range lists crawler operators publish, to check that
    visiting bots are genuine: Google (https://developers.google.com), Microsoft Bing
    (https://www.bing.com), OpenAI (https://openai.com), Perplexity (https://www.perplexity.ai),
    Apple (https://search.developer.apple.com), DuckDuckGo (https://duckduckgo.com), Common Crawl
    (https://index.commoncrawl.org), Anthropic (https://claude.com), Ahrefs (https://api.ahrefs.com)
    and Mistral AI (https://mistral.ai). These are read-only downloads, once a day; no data about your site is sent.
    To show which network a crawler request came from, the IP address of that crawler request (never
    a human visitor’s) is looked up in Team Cymru’s public IP-to-ASN DNS service
    (origin.asn.cymru.com) or, if that fails, in the public internet registries through
    https://rdap.org. Only the crawler IP address is sent.

* Google Privacy Policy
* Microsoft Privacy Statement
* OpenAI Privacy Policy
* Perplexity Privacy Policy
* Apple Privacy Policy
* DuckDuckGo Privacy Policy
* Common Crawl Privacy Policy
* Anthropic Privacy Policy
* Ahrefs Privacy Policy
* Mistral AI Privacy Policy
* Team Cymru IP-to-ASN service
* Team Cymru Privacy Policy
* rdap.org

  1. Google PageSpeed Insights API (https://www.googleapis.com/pagespeedonline/v5/runPagespeed):
    Used for Core Web Vitals and page-speed reports. Contacted only after you add your own
    PageSpeed Insights API key in Settings. The public URL of the page being tested and your
    API key are sent – never page content or visitor data.

* Google APIs Terms of Service
* Google Privacy Policy

  1. Google Fonts (https://fonts.googleapis.com):
    When you generate an Elementor page from a design that uses Google Fonts, that page loads
    the chosen font stylesheets from Google Fonts on the front end. Visitors’ browsers then
    request the fonts from Google, which receives their IP address. Pages that were not
    generated with Google Fonts never contact this service.

* Google Fonts Privacy FAQ
* Google Privacy Policy

  1. Google Search status feed (https://status.search.google.com/incidents.json):
    While the Google services module is on, the plugin downloads Google’s public Search status
    feed about once an hour, so Google updates and outages show on your Overview and charts.
    It is a read-only download; nothing about your site is sent.

* Google Privacy Policy

  1. Websites your pages link to (broken link checks):
    While Broken links is on (it is on by default), the plugin checks the links in your
    published posts and pages in the background, a few at a time and never more than two per
    website in each run. For a link to another website it requests only that link’s address
    (a HEAD request, or a GET for the first kilobyte when HEAD is refused) and records the status
    code. Nothing about your site is sent beyond the request itself, whose user agent names the
    plugin and your site’s address. Addresses on private networks are never requested. Turn off
    “Check links to other sites” under SEO Audit → Links, list sites to skip there, or
    turn the module off in Settings → Modules.

  2. Google tag (gtag.js) (https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js):
    Only if you switch on “Install tracking tag” in Settings → Connections (off by default), your
    pages load Google’s tag with your Google Analytics measurement ID. Visitors’ browsers then send
    page views and the events you chose (phone and email clicks, form submissions, shop sales) to
    Google Analytics, which receives their IP address and browser details. Visitors in the EU, the UK
    and Switzerland are measured without cookies until they accept in your consent banner. No email
    address, phone number or name is ever sent in an event.

* Google Analytics Terms of Service
* Google Privacy Policy

  1. Video sites you embed (video schema) (YouTube, Vimeo, Dailymotion and the other video sites WordPress embeds):
    When a page has an embedded video and automatic video schema is on (it is on by default), the
    plugin asks that video site for the video’s public title, description, thumbnail and length,
    using WordPress’s own embed (oEmbed) client, so it can describe the video for search engines.
    Only the video’s address is sent. This also runs once in the background for pages published
    before the plugin was installed. Answers are saved with the page and refreshed about once a month.
    Turn it off with the video schema switch, or set a Video type on the page yourself.

* YouTube Terms of Service
* Google Privacy Policy
* Vimeo Privacy Policy
* Dailymotion Privacy Policy
sections.installation:
From your WordPress dashboard

  1. Go to Plugins → Add New Plugin.
  2. Search for “Digispot AI”.
  3. Click Install Now, then Activate.

Manual upload

  1. Download the plugin zip from WordPress.org.
  2. Go to Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin, choose the zip and click Install Now.
  3. Activate the plugin.

After activation

  1. You land on the Digispot AI Overview. Click Complete the setup wizard in the welcome banner or the getting-started checklist.
  2. Import data: if Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress or Redirection is installed, import its SEO data and redirects in one click.
  3. Site audit: run your first audit to get a health score for every page.
  4. AI provider: paste your own OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini or DeepSeek key, or connect a Digispot account. You can skip this and add it later.
  5. Connect Google from Settings → Connections → Google Services to see Search Console and GA4 data.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Digispot AI account?

No. The audit, schema, local SEO, redirects, 404 monitor, sitemaps, crawl log, AI referrals and Search Console and GA4 reports all work without an account. For AI fixes, either paste your own OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or DeepSeek key, or connect a Digispot account to use managed AI credits instead.

Can I import my SEO data from Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress or Redirection?

Yes. Go to Settings → Migration, or use the Import step in the setup wizard. It imports meta titles and descriptions, focus keywords, canonical URLs, robots settings, Open Graph and Twitter fields, schema JSON-LD, global settings and redirects. It is safe to run more than once, and it never overwrites data you have already set in Digispot AI.

Can I run it alongside Yoast, Rank Math, AIOSEO or SEOPress?

Yes. Digispot AI detects those plugins and suppresses its own conflicting output, such as canonical URLs and Open Graph tags, so nothing is duplicated. That lets you audit your site and compare before you switch. Once you have imported your data, we recommend keeping one SEO plugin active.

Will it slow down my site?

Audits run in small background batches, not on page load. The crawl log and llms.txt are off until you turn them on in Settings → Modules, and you can switch off any module you do not use.

Does it work with the Classic editor and Elementor?

Yes. The SEO panel appears as a sidebar in the block editor, as a meta box under the Classic editor, and inside the Elementor editor. Audits score the rendered page, so Elementor content is analysed correctly.

Can I use my own AI API key?

Yes. Under Settings → AI Provider choose OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or DeepSeek and paste your key. Content is sent only to the provider you pick, and only when you run an AI action.

How do I connect Google Search Console and Analytics?

Settings → Connections → Google Services, then connect with Google. Sign in and grant access. There is no Client ID or Cloud project to set up. Data is cached in your WordPress database.

Can an AI agent change my site without me knowing?

No. Agents only see the tools you share, and by default every change waits for your approval with a before-and-after preview. Each agent has change limits, your key pages can be protected, you get an email when a new agent connects, and every change is logged and can be undone in one click.

What is llms.txt and do I need it?

llms.txt is a plain-text index at the root of your site that tells AI crawlers what your site is about and which pages matter. Digispot AI generates it from your published content and keeps it up to date. It is optional: turn it on in Settings → Modules.

How does the crawl log know a bot is real?

Googlebot, Bingbot, GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot, Applebot, DuckDuckBot, CCBot, AhrefsBot and MistralAI-User are checked against the IP ranges their operators publish, and Meta’s crawlers against Meta’s network. A request that claims to be one of them from any other IP is marked as spoofed, and the log shows which network and country it really came from, so you can see who is faking crawlers. Crawlers with no public way to verify them are shown as claimed. If you switch on “Block fake crawlers”, requests that claim to be a crawler with a published IP list but come from elsewhere are refused; real crawlers and visitors are never blocked.

Should I redirect every 404?

No. The 404 monitor separates real missing content from bot scanners and exploit probes. Redirect genuine moved pages with one click, and let probe traffic keep returning 404, which is what Google recommends.

What happens to my SEO data if I delete the plugin?

Deleting Digispot AI does not remove your SEO titles, descriptions, focus keywords, schema, redirects or local SEO data by default, so a reinstall picks them up again. Audit caches, Google sync tables and API keys are removed. If you need a complete wipe, contact support and we’ll walk you through it.

Where did my Digispot AI menu items go after updating?

Version 1.0.3 groups the menu by the work you do: Overview, SEO Audit, Search & AI, Analytics, Search Appearance, Technical SEO, Crawl Log, AI Agent (MCP) and Settings. AI fixes are in SEO Audit → Issues, titles, schema, local SEO and llms.txt are in Search Appearance, and keywords are in Search & AI. A one-time note at the top of Digispot AI shows where each moved screen now lives, and old links and bookmarks still open the right screen.

What is Digispot AI Pro?

An add-on that adds rank tracking, AI answer tracking, competitors and backlinks to Search & AI. It is included in every paid Digispot AI plan, with no separate purchase. The rest of this plugin works without it.

Is my site’s data used to train AI models?

No. Page content is sent to an AI provider only when you run an AI action, and only to the provider you configured. See Third-Party Services above for exactly what is sent to whom.
sections.changelog:
1.0.4

  • Clearer keyword actions: “Save” adds a search to Your keywords (free) and “Remove” takes it off the list, while “Track rank” always means checking its Google position in Rankings.
  • Keywords › Potential: each Search Console search can be sent to Rankings in one click, as in Google Insights and the Overview quick wins.
  • Keywords: Discover now sits with the other Keywords tabs, and links from Rankings open it with the keyword already filled in.
  • The Keywords page only mentions AI answers when Digispot AI Pro is installed.

1.0.3

  • New: an Overview answers how the site is doing in search, what to fix next and where it is heading: a plain-language summary of risks and wins, clicks, searches, pages in Google, visits by channel, device and city, the next fixes ranked by impact, both health scores, quick-win searches and daily trends. It reads only data already on your site, so it opens instantly and works with whatever you have connected.
  • New: the Overview also shows what only your site knows: Googlebot, Bingbot and AI crawler visits, visits from AI assistants, sitemap size and IndexNow submissions, SEO fixes made this month, thin pages and heading problems, unresolved 404s and redirects, how many pages have their own title, description and schema, and your last import. Each number opens the exact list behind it.
  • New: a Search & AI section brings Keywords, Rankings and AI Visibility together as one flow. Keywords opens on Overview, Your keywords, Potential (Search Console searches you are not tracking yet, added in one click) and Check a keyword. Old links and bookmarks still open the right screen.
  • New: Search Console searches in Google Insights and the Overview quick wins can be sent to Rankings in one click, and Your keywords points to Rankings when nothing is tracked there yet. Rankings is part of Digispot AI Pro, included in every paid Digispot AI plan; keywords open in its Add dialog and nothing is checked until you confirm.
  • Faster: saving a post no longer waits for the sitemap to rebuild. Changes made close together are gathered into one background update about a minute later, and large sites build their sitemaps in small batches.
  • Lighter pages: fewer database reads on every visit (redirects, site title and settings), and lower background load on quiet sites.
  • Faster admin: Digispot screens load only what they show, so the first screen opens with about a fifth of the download. Search Console syncs fetch each report once instead of once per hundred pages, and “Sync now” and the main image speed test run in the background, so they no longer stop at your host’s time limit.
  • Smaller database: site-wide audits no longer store a copy of every page in your options table, and copies left by earlier versions are cleared after the update. Audits and Google checks no longer wake the site every minute when there is nothing to do.
  • Easier to find your way: the Digispot AI menu is reorganised so each tool sits with the work it belongs to. After the update, a one-time note at the top of Digispot AI shows where each moved screen now lives, and old links and bookmarks still work.

1.0.2

  • New: connect Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or VS Code with one link. Paste your site’s AI agent address into the app, approve it in wp-admin and it is connected. No application password to copy and nothing to install.
  • New: when you approve an app, choose what it may do (read your SEO data, or read and make SEO changes), how long the access lasts (1 day, 30 days or until you revoke it), and whether it works as an SEO auditor or with full access to redirects and Digispot settings.
  • New: API tokens for automations that cannot open a browser (scripts, workflow tools, the OpenAI API), with ready-to-copy setup snippets.
  • New: “Add to Cursor” and “Add to VS Code” buttons, and a Claude Code command that works in Windows PowerShell and Command Prompt too.
  • New: AI agent access can stay on until you turn it off, and you get an email reminder before a timed access window ends.
  • Connected apps are listed in AI Agent (MCP) → Activity, where you can change an app’s access level or revoke it in one click. Every app stays under your approvals, limits, protected pages, activity log and undo.
  • When an agent account isn’t allowed to manage redirects or site settings, the agent now tells you exactly where to change that.
  • AI provider model lists updated to the current models. A model you saved that is no longer offered moves to its closest current equivalent instead of the default.

1.0.1

  • New: the crawl log shows where every crawler request came from: the official crawler list it matches, or the network, hosting company and country behind it. It now checks 15 published crawler IP lists (Google, Bing, OpenAI, Perplexity, Apple, DuckDuckGo, Common Crawl, Ahrefs, Mistral) and Meta’s network, lists the networks sending fake crawlers, and lets you look up any IP from your server logs.
  • New: internal link suggestions. Each page’s report shows where it should link and which pages should link to it, with the exact sentence and words to use, taken from your focus keywords, the searches your pages earn and their titles. Add a link in one click and undo it from the change history. Your editor shows the same ideas with a Copy link button.
  • New: keyword tracking, free. Pick the keywords you care about (or add all your focus keywords in one click) and see where you rank on Google, your clicks and impressions, what moved since last period and a history line, straight from your Search Console. History is kept for a year.
  • New: SEO report by email (off until you turn it on in Settings → Modules). Weekly, every two weeks or monthly: clicks and position against last time, your tracked keywords that moved most, pages losing clicks, the fixes you made, index and site health, and one thing to do next. Preview it or send yourself a test first.
  • New: image alt and title text from templates. Images without alt text get one from the image’s file name, or the page title when the file has a camera name like IMG_2034, and you can change the wording in Titles & meta → Images. Your media library’s alt text always wins, images you marked decorative by hand keep their empty alt text, and the audit now shows which images still need real alt text.
  • New: broken links, free. Every link in your posts and pages is checked in the background, internal and external, and Technical SEO → Broken links lists the broken and redirected ones with the pages that use them. Change the address, remove the link or add a redirect in one click, with undo. Sites that block automated checks are shown as “could not verify”, never as broken, and your weekly report and Site health count what is left to fix.
  • New: install your Google Analytics tag with one switch in Settings → Connections (off until you turn it on). The measurement ID fills in from your connected Analytics, consent is handled for visitors in Europe, your own visits are not counted, and phone and email clicks, form submissions and shop sales are recorded too. If another plugin already adds the tag, Digispot tells you and stays out of the way.
  • New: main image priority. When a page’s largest image loads late, its report names the image and why, and one click makes it load first and stops it being lazy-loaded, with a before-and-after speed test. Choose the image yourself on any page, or make the featured image the main image for a whole post type. Digispot steps aside when a speed plugin already manages image loading.
  • New: show your address, phone, opening hours and a map on your pages with four blocks (or shortcodes) that use the details you already saved in Local SEO. Opening hours highlight today and say whether you are open now, the map loads only when a visitor clicks, and businesses with several locations get a list with a search box and a “Near me” button that sorts them by distance, with no map key needed. Businesses that visit customers never show their street address.
  • New: automatic video schema. Pages with a YouTube, Vimeo or other video get video schema with the video’s own title, thumbnail, length and date, kept up to date as videos are added or removed, so they can appear in Google’s video results. A Video type you set on a page always wins, and one switch turns it off.
  • Video sitemap: uses each video’s own title, description and length, and leaves out videos without a thumbnail image, which Google rejects.
  • New: redirect scheduling. Give a redirect a start and end date for a sale or a seasonal page, and it switches itself on and off at the right minute, even without WordPress’s scheduled tasks. Label redirects with groups, filter by group or state (scheduled, active, expired, paused), and enable, pause, move or delete many at once.
  • New: export all redirects to a spreadsheet (CSV) and import them back. The import shows what will be added, changed or skipped (and why) before anything is saved, and the whole import can be undone in one click from the change history.
  • New: Auto links (off until you turn it on in Settings → Modules). Choose words once and they link to the right page wherever they appear, up to 3 per page and never in headings or existing links. Your content is not changed; the links are added when the page is shown.
  • New: WP-CLI commands (wp digispot) to audit pages, edit titles and descriptions, undo changes, manage redirects, rebuild sitemaps, and import from another SEO plugin or undo that import.
  • New: “Your business” step in setup. Digispot reads the business details your site already shows (and your previous SEO plugin’s settings), you confirm them, and your business schema, local checks and AI fixes use them. Paste a Google Maps link instead of looking up coordinates.
  • Local SEO now supports businesses that visit customers (your street address stays private and the areas you serve are listed) and online-only businesses, and asks only for what search engines need.
  • Business types now always produce valid schema, whatever language your admin is in.
  • New: works with Polylang. Every language version keeps its own canonical, social locale and sitemap links, and the site title shows in the visitor’s language.
  • AI fixes are written in the page’s language, and readability checks judge each page in its own language.
  • New: undo an import from Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress or Redirection with one click. Every title, description, keyword, setting and redirect it brought in goes back to what it was, and anything you edited since is kept unless you choose otherwise. You can also choose to replace values you already set instead of keeping them.
  • New: WooCommerce product pages get complete product rich-result data — sale prices, stock, reviews, every variation, shipping cost and return terms — plus product social tags, a Shop page you can optimise, optional shorter product and category URLs, and a suggested redirect when a product is unpublished.
  • New: schema builder in the editor — 23 schema types (articles, products, reviews, recipes, events, jobs, videos, courses, software, books, people, services, FAQ, how-to and page types like About and Contact). Fields fill themselves from the page, and a live preview checks the markup for Google rich results before you save.
  • New: schema templates — give whole groups of pages the right schema type at once, by post type, category, tag, URL or page, and see how many pages each template covers.
  • New: FAQ, How-to and Table of Contents blocks. FAQ and How-to content is added to the page’s schema automatically; the table of contents keeps itself up to date.
  • Schema now links each page, its author and your business into one connected graph, with author profiles (bio and social links from Users → Profile), About/Contact page types, and archive and search pages marked up too.
  • When another SEO plugin is active, Digispot no longer adds a second schema graph next to its own.
  • New: Titles & meta — set the search title and description once for each type of page (posts, pages, products, categories, archives, search) with variables like %title% and %sitename%, and hide whole page types from search. Nothing changes until you save a template.
  • New: choose a primary category for posts (and WooCommerce products). Breadcrumbs, category links and schema use it, and it is imported from Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO and SEOPress.
  • New: “Don’t update the modified date” when you save a small fix, so search engines keep seeing your last real update.
  • New: Breadcrumbs block for the block editor, and automatic breadcrumbs for themes that support them.
  • New: SEO menu in the admin bar on your pages: score and grade, the page report, Edit SEO, and one-click Rich Results and PageSpeed checks.
  • New: let AI agents like Claude fix your on-page SEO safely — titles, descriptions, focus keywords, H1s, image alt text, canonicals and redirects — with a preview you approve, change limits, protected pages, email alerts, a pause button per agent and one-click undo. Agents can also look up keyword demand and Core Web Vitals through your Digispot Cloud connection.
  • New: create a dedicated account for an AI agent in one click. It gets the SEO Manager role and its own password, so you can revoke it without touching your own login. Download the agent activity log as a spreadsheet (CSV), hide the last part of IP addresses for privacy, and log the real agent IP behind Cloudflare or your own proxy.
  • AI agents: get an email when a connected agent starts calling from a new network, see each agent’s session in the activity log, and turn the whole AI Agent feature off in Settings → Modules.
  • AI agents: Digispot now has its own agent connection address that lists only its SEO tools; agents set up on 1.0.0 keep working. Changes an agent proposes to page content show only the words that change, and each agent has a daily cap on Digispot Cloud lookups.
  • AI agents: try them on a local copy of your site (localhost, .test, .local) with one switch. It turns itself off if the site is moved to a real domain.
  • New: AI visibility overview under AI SEO: which AI crawlers can reach your site, your llms.txt, and the visits AI assistants send you.
  • llms.txt follows the published format, lists the same pages as your XML sitemap and can include an llms-full.txt with your pages’ text. robots.txt separates AI search crawlers from AI training crawlers, and AI referrals now also count DeepSeek, Grok, Meta AI, Le Chat and Microsoft 365 Copilot.
  • New: SEO change history — every change to titles, descriptions, robots, canonicals, schema and image alt text is listed, whoever made it (you, a bulk edit, AI, a one-click fix, an import or an AI agent), and can be undone in one click. Find it under SEO Audit and on each page’s report.
  • New: Content overview and page list — thin pages, heading problems, the phrases you use most and what each page is for, with a list of pages to fix first. Free, read on your site.
  • Orphan pages (no internal links pointing to them) are now detected on existing sites too, so some pages may drop a few points on their next check. Pages in your site navigation never count as orphans.
  • Team members who can edit only pages can now use the SEO panel, schema and AI tools on those pages.
  • Editors who are not admins can save pages again when the SEO panel is open (the site-wide schema it shows no longer blocks the save).
  • New: Site Graph (beta) in Content — see how your pages connect, and find orphan pages, topic groups without a main page, and focus keywords that don’t match real searches. You can also ask Claude about your site structure (read-only).
  • The admin screens and editor panels can now be translated into your language, including audit findings, module names and messages from the server.
  • SEO Audit now holds your one list of pages, with search, score, issue and search-demand filters.
  • The AI Fixes menu is now called AI SEO, matching the screens inside it.
  • New Crawl cleanup: attachment pages and comment-reply links now go to the right page, with optional clean-up of tracking parameters, feeds, head links, spam searches and the /category/ prefix.
  • Sitemaps now read as a tidy page in your browser, and a new HTML sitemap block lists your content for visitors.
  • Core Web Vitals moved to Performance.
  • The live SEO score while you edit now matches the saved audit on pages with breadcrumbs.
  • Your SEO score and fixes now work inside Elementor and Beaver Builder, and heading fixes change the builder’s own layout.
  • Pages built with Divi, Bricks or WPBakery say clearly which fixes need the builder, right on the page report and in bulk fixes.
  • Image sitemaps now include images from builder layouts.
  • Search Console diagnostics now recognise pages you set to noindex in Digispot.
  • Brand: admin menu, editor and Elementor icons now use the same Digispot AI mark as the WordPress.org listing.
  • Migration banner: clearer feature list.
  • SEO tags now appear on your blog home, category, tag, author and archive pages too (description and canonical link), on every theme.
  • After Digispot changes a page it clears your page cache and checks the live page, and tells you if your theme or cache is still showing the old version.
  • New Theme & Cache settings: fix themes that override your titles with one click, clear your page cache, headless support.
  • Admin bar warns you when a page, or the whole site, is hidden from search engines.
  • SEO tags now follow your WordPress “discourage search engines” setting even when a page has its own robots setting.
  • When another SEO plugin (Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress or The SEO Framework) is active, Digispot now leaves all SEO tags to it, so pages never get two titles.
  • Digispot AI permissions show as their own group in Members and User Role Editor.
  • The Digispot AI screens now fit properly on phones.
  • Switching from All in One SEO, SEOPress or the Redirection plugin? Import your titles, descriptions, keywords, social cards, redirects, site description and Google verification in one step, with a clear report of what came over and what didn’t.
  • Imports now resume where they stopped, work on very large sites, and never overwrite what you already set in Digispot.
  • The Setup Wizard finds SEO data from your previous plugin even when that plugin is switched off.
  • Running two SEO plugins? Digispot tells you which one controls your SEO tags and walks you through importing, then switching the old one off. Its data is kept.
  • The Facebook and X titles, descriptions and images you set for a page now appear on your site.
  • New redirects imported from Rank Math “starts with” and “contains” rules now send visitors to the exact target page (redirects already imported by an earlier version are left as they are; re-import after removing them to pick up the fix).
  • On Genesis themes, Digispot now prints your SEO tags and keeps your Genesis page settings.
  • Your blog page now uses the SEO title and robots setting you gave it.
  • Fixed: an old bookmark or link to a Digispot AI admin page from before the navigation redesign could show a “not allowed” error instead of opening the plugin.
  • Your SEO score now updates as you write, in both the block editor and the classic editor, and lines up with the full audit after you save.
  • Focus keyword can now be set right from the block editor’s SEO panel.
  • Unpublished pages are checked against the web address they will have once published, so the score you see while drafting matches the score after you publish.
  • The audit’s conflicting-SEO-plugin warning now also names SEOPress.
  • Your page reports now group checks into packs (On-page SEO, Content, Readability, Technical, Schema, Social sharing, Performance) with a score for each, so you can see at a glance where a page needs work.
  • New Site health score on the Dashboard: site-wide checks (HTTPS, sitemap, analytics) are now checked once for your whole site instead of on every single page.
  • Turn any audit pack on or off in Settings > Modules to match what you actually need checked.
  • Optional email alert (off by default) when Site health finds a critical site-wide issue.
  • Site-wide checks (HTTPS, sitemap, analytics) now appear once under Site health instead of on every page, so most pages will score a few points lower on their next check — nothing to fix, those checks still run under Site health.
  • Site health now checks visibility, robots.txt, sitemap, SSL, redirects, updates and AI-crawler access, with one-click fixes.
  • New on-page checks: keyword cannibalisation, duplicate titles, orphan pages, indexability conflicts, readability.
  • Overall score is now weighted by pack; scores may move a little on the next check.
  • New checks for AI answer engines (question-and-answer pages, FAQ schema, clear author/date), AI search visibility (server-rendered content, citations, freshness), and local SEO (matching business name/address/phone, click-to-call links, duplicate locations).
  • A pack with nothing to check on a page (for example, local SEO checks on a page that isn’t a location) no longer shows a confusing “0” score.
  • Heading fixes now work safely on Spectra, Kadence Blocks and GenerateBlocks headings, and tell you when a heading has to be changed in the editor.
  • Heading and text fixes no longer affect block styles or settings.
  • Pages built with SiteOrigin Page Builder are recognised, and their images now appear in your image sitemap.
  • Beaver Builder: the H1 fix now works whether your theme shows the page title or not.
  • Privacy: password-protected posts no longer show their text in search descriptions, schema or video and news sitemaps.
  • Redirects: switching a redirect back on can no longer create a redirect loop, and home-page redirects created by mistake for posts with non-English addresses are paused.
  • Imported and edited SEO data keeps quotes, backslashes and non-English keywords intact, and undo restores builder layouts exactly.
  • Opening hours in your business schema use the format Google accepts, including “24 Hours” and split hours.
  • Search Console numbers add up across every address of a page, long page addresses are matched to their posts, and the SEO Audit list shows clicks, impressions and CTR.
  • Digispot leaves robots.txt and the sitemap address to another SEO plugin while that plugin is in charge.
  • AI fixes are added to your page only when you accept them, and an empty AI answer never replaces your text.
  • Requires WordPress 6.2 or later.

1.0.0

  • Initial release on the WordPress Plugin Directory.

short_description: Audit every page, fix issues in bulk with AI, add schema and local SEO, and let Claude or Cursor work on your SEO through MCP.
description:
Audit every page. Fix issues in bulk with AI. Let Claude or Cursor work on your SEO, with your approval. All inside wp-admin, free.

Search now happens in Google and in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude and Copilot. Digispot AI helps you win both.

→ See it: the Overview

✔ Free, no account needed

  • AI agents (MCP) that propose SEO fixes for your approval, with one-click undo
  • Bulk AI fixes with your own OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini or DeepSeek key
  • Keyword tracking from your own Search Console
  • Broken link checker and internal link suggestions
  • SEO change history with one-click undo for every change
  • Multi-location local SEO with LocalBusiness schema
  • Verified crawl log that catches fake Googlebots, and can block them if you choose
  • AI referrals from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Mode, Gemini and Copilot
  • Smart 404 monitor and unlimited redirects

Several of these are paid add-ons in other SEO plugins.

Overview: your site at a glance

  • A plain-language summary of what is going well and what needs attention
  • Clicks, searches by position, pages in Google, visits and key events, each compared with the previous 28 days
  • The next fixes ranked by impact, with site health and page audit scores side by side
  • Crawler visits, AI assistant visits, fixes made this month and unresolved 404s, each opening the exact list behind it

→ See it: the Overview

Switching from Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress or Redirection?

Import titles, descriptions, keywords, canonicals, robots, social fields, schema and redirects in one click. Safe to re-run. Never overwrites what you already set, and one click undoes the whole import.

→ See it: one-click migration

AI Agent (MCP): your AI assistant, your rules

  • Connect Claude, Cursor or another MCP app in a few steps, with a dedicated agent account you can revoke anytime
  • Agents read your audit, Search Console and Site Graph data, then propose fixes: titles, descriptions, alt text, internal links, redirects and schema
  • Every change waits for your approval with a before-and-after preview, unless you choose otherwise
  • Guardrails: change limits per agent, protected pages, email alerts and a full activity log

→ See it: agent approvals

SEO Audit: a score for every page

  • 75+ checks per page (grouped into audit packs), from meta tags and headings to speed, HTTPS and schema
  • Scores the rendered page, so Elementor and page-builder content counts
  • One ranked list of the issues costing you the most, across every page, under SEO Audit → Issues
  • Change history: every SEO change, whoever made it, with one-click undo

→ See it: the SEO audit · → See it: change history

AI Fixes: one click, you review

Fix issues straight from SEO Audit → Issues.

  • Titles, descriptions, focus keywords, alt text, schema, canonicals and H1s
  • Fix one page or every affected page at once
  • See each suggestion next to the current value. Nothing saves until you click Apply.

→ See it: bulk AI fixes

Search Console and GA4, inside WordPress

  • One-click Google connection, no Client ID to paste
  • Clicks, impressions, CTR and position next to GA4 sessions and channels, under Analytics → Google Insights
  • Keyword tracking in Search & AI → Keywords: pick your keywords and see position, clicks and what moved, free
  • SEO report by email, weekly or monthly (turn on in Settings → Modules)

→ See it: keyword tracking · → See it: Google Insights

Links that work for you

  • Internal link suggestions with the exact sentence and words, added in one click
  • Broken links checked in the background, with one-click fixes, under SEO Audit → Links
  • Site Structure (beta): see topic clusters, pillar pages and orphan pages on one map

→ See it: link suggestions · → See it: broken links · → See it: Site Structure

Search Appearance: titles, schema and local SEO

Everything you set once for how the site shows in search lives in Search Appearance: titles and meta templates, site identity and schema, local SEO and llms.txt.

  • Organization or LocalBusiness (55 types), WebSite, BreadcrumbList and page schema like Article, Product, FAQ, HowTo and Video
  • One profile per location with hours, services and payments
  • Graph, list and raw JSON-LD views with one-click copy

→ See it: schema markup · → See it: local SEO profiles

Editor panel

  • Live SEO score, focus and secondary keywords, snippet preview and social cards
  • “Generate with AI” for title and description
  • Works in the block editor, Classic editor, Elementor and Quick Edit

→ See it: the editor panel

Built for AI search

  • Search & AI → AI Visibility: which AI crawlers can reach you, AI visits, llms.txt and agent access on one screen
  • See every crawler visit: Googlebot, Bingbot, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and more
  • Crawlers verified against their published IP lists, so fakes are flagged with the network and country they really came from
  • See humans arriving from AI answers, with landing page and query
  • Auto-generated llms.txt (turn on in Settings → Modules)

→ See it: AI visibility · → See it: the verified crawl log · → See it: AI referrals

Technical SEO, handled

  • Redirects: 301, 302, 307, 308, 410 and 451, regex-capable, with hit counts, scheduling and CSV import/export
  • 404 monitor that separates real missing pages from bot probes
  • XML sitemaps, robots.txt editor, IndexNow, breadcrumbs and automatic image alt text

→ See it: redirects and the 404 monitor

For teams

  • Setup wizard: import, first audit and AI provider in a few steps
  • “SEO Manager” role for editors, without full admin access
  • Runs side by side with Yoast, Rank Math, AIOSEO or SEOPress without duplicate tags
  • WP-CLI commands for audits, SEO fields, redirects and undo
  • Turn modules on or off to load only what you use

Works with your stack

WordPress 6.2+, PHP 7.4+, block editor, Classic editor, WooCommerce and Elementor.

Free vs. Digispot Cloud

Everything above is free and runs in your WordPress site, including the AI agent, its approvals and undo. A free Digispot AI account adds managed AI credits (no AI key needed) and cloud lookups: search demand, Core Web Vitals field data and domain age.

Digispot AI Pro adds rank tracking, AI answer tracking, competitors, backlinks and exact keyword data to Search & AI, and gives your AI agent read-only tools for that data. Pro is a separate add-on, included in every paid Digispot AI plan with no separate purchase. You can hide its tabs in Settings → Pro.

Trademarks

Rank Math, Yoast SEO, All in One SEO (AIOSEO), SEOPress, WooCommerce, Elementor, Google, Google Search Console, Google Analytics, ChatGPT, OpenAI, Anthropic, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Microsoft Copilot, Bing and DeepSeek are trademarks of their respective owners. They are named only to describe compatibility, data import and integrations. Digispot AI is not affiliated with, sponsored by or endorsed by any of them.

Third-Party Services

This plugin relies on the following third-party services. Each entry states what is
sent and when. No data leaves your site until you connect or configure the relevant
service.

  1. Digispot AI API (https://api.digispot.ai, keyword and search data on https://app.digispot.ai, OAuth proxy https://wordpress.digispot.ai):
    Powers managed AI generation, rank tracking, backlink data, and the free lookups (keyword
    demand, Chrome UX Report web vitals, domain age, PageSpeed). Page content, titles, and prompts
    are sent only when you run an AI action or a cloud-backed report; keywords you research or set
    as focus keywords, your Search Console query strings, and your site’s URLs are sent only for
    those lookups. All of this happens only after you connect a Digispot account, and answers are
    cached in your WordPress database to avoid repeat calls. Every request from a connected site
    also carries your site’s address (domain), its Site Title and the plugin and WordPress version
    numbers, so your account can tell its connected sites apart. The OAuth proxy is contacted only during Google sign-in,
    so you never have to paste a Google Client ID. When an AI app connects with one-URL sign-in and your host
    keeps /.well-known away from WordPress, the app is pointed to the same host, which reads this site’s
    public sign-in details (endpoint addresses only); approvals and tokens stay on your site.

* Digispot Terms of Service
* Digispot Privacy Policy

  1. Google APIs (OAuth 2.0):
    Displays your Search Console, Analytics 4 (including visits by channel and city), and Business Profile data. Contacted only after
    you complete the Google OAuth flow. Retrieved data is stored locally in your WordPress
    database to speed up loading. Hosts used: accounts.google.com (sign-in),
    www.googleapis.com (Search Console), analyticsdata.googleapis.com and
    analyticsadmin.googleapis.com (Analytics 4), mybusiness.googleapis.com,
    mybusinessaccountmanagement.googleapis.com,
    mybusinessbusinessinformation.googleapis.com and
    businessprofileperformance.googleapis.com (Business Profile).

* Google Privacy Policy
* Google Terms of Service

  1. AI providers (opt-in, bring your own key):
    Digispot AI supports using your own API key with an external AI provider instead of the
    managed Digispot service. No content is sent to any of these providers until you
    explicitly select one and enter your own API key.     When enabled, the content you ask the
    plugin to optimize (such as a post title, excerpt, or body) is sent to the provider you
    chose:

* OpenAI – https://api.openai.com – Terms | Privacy
* Anthropic – https://api.anthropic.com – Terms | Privacy
* Google Gemini – https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com – Terms | Privacy
* DeepSeek – https://api.deepseek.com – Terms | Privacy

  1. IndexNow (https://api.indexnow.org):
    If you enable IndexNow, the URLs of posts you publish or update are POSTed to the IndexNow
    API so participating search engines can recrawl them. Only URLs and your generated
    IndexNow key are sent – never page content.

* IndexNow Documentation and Terms

  1. Anonymous usage telemetry (opt-in, OFF by default) (https://api.digispot.ai):
    If — and only if — you switch this on in the plugin settings, Digispot AI reports three
    lifecycle events (plugin activated, deactivated, uninstalled) so we can see how many sites
    use the plugin and why people stop. When you deactivate, you may optionally pick a reason;
    that reason is sent with the event. Nothing is sent while this setting is off, which is
    how it ships.     What is sent: an opaque random install identifier, the event name, and the
    plugin, WordPress and PHP version numbers. What is never sent: your site URL, your email,
    usernames, post content, or any other data that identifies you or your site.

* Digispot Terms of Service
* Digispot Privacy Policy

  1. Crawler IP range lists and IP network lookups (crawl log module only):
    The crawl log module downloads the IP-range lists crawler operators publish, to check that
    visiting bots are genuine: Google (https://developers.google.com), Microsoft Bing
    (https://www.bing.com), OpenAI (https://openai.com), Perplexity (https://www.perplexity.ai),
    Apple (https://search.developer.apple.com), DuckDuckGo (https://duckduckgo.com), Common Crawl
    (https://index.commoncrawl.org), Anthropic (https://claude.com), Ahrefs (https://api.ahrefs.com)
    and Mistral AI (https://mistral.ai). These are read-only downloads, once a day; no data about your site is sent.
    To show which network a crawler request came from, the IP address of that crawler request (never
    a human visitor’s) is looked up in Team Cymru’s public IP-to-ASN DNS service
    (origin.asn.cymru.com) or, if that fails, in the public internet registries through
    https://rdap.org. Only the crawler IP address is sent.

* Google Privacy Policy
* Microsoft Privacy Statement
* OpenAI Privacy Policy
* Perplexity Privacy Policy
* Apple Privacy Policy
* DuckDuckGo Privacy Policy
* Common Crawl Privacy Policy
* Anthropic Privacy Policy
* Ahrefs Privacy Policy
* Mistral AI Privacy Policy
* Team Cymru IP-to-ASN service
* Team Cymru Privacy Policy
* rdap.org

  1. Google PageSpeed Insights API (https://www.googleapis.com/pagespeedonline/v5/runPagespeed):
    Used for Core Web Vitals and page-speed reports. Contacted only after you add your own
    PageSpeed Insights API key in Settings. The public URL of the page being tested and your
    API key are sent – never page content or visitor data.

* Google APIs Terms of Service
* Google Privacy Policy

  1. Google Fonts (https://fonts.googleapis.com):
    When you generate an Elementor page from a design that uses Google Fonts, that page loads
    the chosen font stylesheets from Google Fonts on the front end. Visitors’ browsers then
    request the fonts from Google, which receives their IP address. Pages that were not
    generated with Google Fonts never contact this service.

* Google Fonts Privacy FAQ
* Google Privacy Policy

  1. Google Search status feed (https://status.search.google.com/incidents.json):
    While the Google services module is on, the plugin downloads Google’s public Search status
    feed about once an hour, so Google updates and outages show on your Overview and charts.
    It is a read-only download; nothing about your site is sent.

* Google Privacy Policy

  1. Websites your pages link to (broken link checks):
    While Broken links is on (it is on by default), the plugin checks the links in your
    published posts and pages in the background, a few at a time and never more than two per
    website in each run. For a link to another website it requests only that link’s address
    (a HEAD request, or a GET for the first kilobyte when HEAD is refused) and records the status
    code. Nothing about your site is sent beyond the request itself, whose user agent names the
    plugin and your site’s address. Addresses on private networks are never requested. Turn off
    “Check links to other sites” under SEO Audit → Links, list sites to skip there, or
    turn the module off in Settings → Modules.

  2. Google tag (gtag.js) (https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js):
    Only if you switch on “Install tracking tag” in Settings → Connections (off by default), your
    pages load Google’s tag with your Google Analytics measurement ID. Visitors’ browsers then send
    page views and the events you chose (phone and email clicks, form submissions, shop sales) to
    Google Analytics, which receives their IP address and browser details. Visitors in the EU, the UK
    and Switzerland are measured without cookies until they accept in your consent banner. No email
    address, phone number or name is ever sent in an event.

* Google Analytics Terms of Service
* Google Privacy Policy

  1. Video sites you embed (video schema) (YouTube, Vimeo, Dailymotion and the other video sites WordPress embeds):
    When a page has an embedded video and automatic video schema is on (it is on by default), the
    plugin asks that video site for the video’s public title, description, thumbnail and length,
    using WordPress’s own embed (oEmbed) client, so it can describe the video for search engines.
    Only the video’s address is sent. This also runs once in the background for pages published
    before the plugin was installed. Answers are saved with the page and refreshed about once a month.
    Turn it off with the video schema switch, or set a Video type on the page yourself.

* YouTube Terms of Service
* Google Privacy Policy
* Vimeo Privacy Policy
* Dailymotion Privacy Policy
